summary.text: Father of Euphemus (`euphemus-ciconian`), captain of the Ciconian spearmen — attested by Homer as son of Ceas and by Apollodorus among the allies who joined the Trojans after nine years of siege.

story.text: In the Catalogue, Nestor names Euphemus captain of the Ciconian spearmen, the son of Ceas' son Troezenus, nurtured of Zeus — a parentage Homer fixes in the muster-roll though the poet names Troezenus only through his son.

Apollodorus counts Euphemus son of Troezenus among the allies who came to join the Trojans. He must be kept distinct from Troezen the city-founder (`pittheus`' brother in later myth) and from the Argonaut Euphemus son of Poseidon.
